technical_and_design_decisions: For U1, leverage the existing Hortonworks Teradata connector pattern (TeradataConnManager) rather than building a custom JDBC bridge; treat the NPE as a missing default connection-manager resolution in Sqoop's job launcher.
For U2, externalize the logging directory through Spring's property placeholder mechanism (e.g., xd.logging.dir) with a fallback to ${xd.home}/logs to preserve backward compatibility.
For U3, create spring-bus as a new top-level Maven multi-module project; move message-bus code preserving the public API and use Maven dependency inheritance to consume it from Spring XD.
For U4, move the type-conversion service abstractions (Converter, ConversionService wiring) into spring-cloud-dataflow core, exposing a stable SPI that custom modules can implement.
For U5, place the serialization codec in spring-bus alongside message-bus, with a pluggable CodecStrategy interface (Jackson, Kryo, etc.) so XD can inherit via dependency.
For U6, implement the singlenode Admin SPI on top of an in-JVM ModuleLauncher that uses local message channels and an embedded servlet/runtime, suitable for local developer workflows.
For U7, implement the Diego Receptor Admin SPI as a remote ModuleLauncher client using the Receptor/BBS API; modules are submitted as Diego LRPs and registered with the XD message bus.
For U8, evaluate Eureka and Consul as candidate service-discovery backends; produce a small POC and design notes rather than a full production implementation.
assumptions: Each work day is 8 productive hours (no meeting overhead deducted).
The Spring XD, spring-bus (new), and spring-cloud-dataflow source trees already exist locally and build successfully with Maven before work begins.
A single senior developer performs all work end-to-end, so no hand-off overhead is included beyond normal code review/rework already folded into each activity.
Unit tests and integration tests are part of each activity's effort; no separate QA cycle is added.
Java 8 (or 17+ for newer Spring) and the necessary Hortonworks/Teradata, Diego, and Cloud Foundry tooling are available locally or in CI.
Diego Receptor API and CF Lattice are stable and accessible; no platform-team coordination delays are accounted for.
Documentation is limited to release notes and short design notes; no full user-guide or admin-guide rewrite is in scope.
No major architectural surprises or cross-team blockers are encountered during execution.

activities.activity_description: Reproduce the NPE when using the Teradata JDBC driver directly, register org.apache.sqoop.teradata.TeradataConnManager as a known connection-manager (or install the Hortonworks connector), wire it into the Sqoop job launcher, and add integration tests covering import jobs against a Teradata instance.

Introduce an xd.logging.dir (or equivalent) property, plumb it through the logging subsystem (e.g., log4j/logback file appender configuration) with a default of ${xd.home}/logs, and update the RPM/deployment script defaults to point at /var/log/spring-xd.

Create the new spring-bus Maven module(s), relocate the message-bus source code and tests, ensure public API and Spring configuration metadata are preserved, update Spring XD's pom.xml to depend on spring-bus, and verify all existing tests and stream scenarios pass.

Extract input/output type-conversion classes and related SPI into spring-cloud-dataflow, expose a stable module-facing conversion service so custom modules can produce/consume custom domain objects, update Spring XD imports, and re-run module registration/composition tests.

Relocate the serialization codec implementation(s) into spring-bus behind a CodecStrategy abstraction, ensure it composes cleanly with the relocated message-bus, and re-wire Spring XD to depend on the new module while validating bus round-trip behavior.

Design and implement an in-JVM XD Admin SPI backed by a local ModuleLauncher. Use embedded message channels and an embedded container so streams/tasks can be orchestrated locally without an external runtime; provide a launcher entry point and integration tests for representative stream and job modules.

activities.activity_name: Diego Receptor XD Admin SPI implementation (U7)
activities.activity_description: Implement a Diego Receptor-based ModuleLauncher that submits modules as Diego LRPs and tracks their lifecycle, wire it into the XD Admin SPI for CF Lattice/Diego deployments, handle secure Receptor/BBS communication, and test end-to-end stream execution on a Diego environment.

Investigate how spring-cloud-stream modules could self-register with a service-discovery backend, evaluate Eureka and Consul as candidates, build a small proof-of-concept demonstrating discovery and orchestration by the XD runtime on CF, and produce a short design note with recommendations.

Run a full integration pass covering all U1–U8 changes together: end-to-end stream/job execution on the singlenode and Diego launchers, Teradata import via Sqoop, configurable logging, and the new message-bus / type-conversion / codec wiring. Fix any regressions uncovered.

Write concise release notes summarizing the new Teradata support, configurable logging, the spring-bus / spring-cloud-dataflow moves, the new Admin SPI implementations, and the service-discovery findings; update relevant reference docs and changelogs.
